_why: THE SHARE WAS AHEAD OF THE REPO, AND THE PIPELINE WOULD HAVE OVERWRITTEN IT (#1275).
site_a/MANIFEST.json accumulated field values and mature flags that never reached
the committed profile, because they were applied to the per-site file BY HAND.
`populate_archive.py` copies the profile OVER that file, so the next ordinary build
would have deleted one published asset and stripped 1,947 records of 12,096 values.
Measured 2026-08-26 against the live share; `manifest_guard.py` reproduces it.
This document carries that advantage back so the repair is reproducible from the
REPO ALONE. The share is not a dependency of the pipeline: a test that needed it
would pass on a workstation and fail on a runner, which is the same shape as the
bug it is fixing.
⛔ THE PASS THAT APPLIES THIS CAN ONLY ADD, NEVER REPLACE.
added — records present at the share and absent from the profile. Exactly one:
`0407bb0c-…`, 'The Great Wave — rotated scan (EXIF orientation 6)'. A
build would have DELETED it from the published dataset.
fill  — keys the profile does not hold, or holds empty. 12,096 values across
1,947 records: 10,145 `field_values` entries (100 records had none at
all), 1,947 explicit `mature: false` flags, and 4 `metadata.sha256` keys.
⚠️ WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. 160 `file_size_bytes` and 6 `metadata.sha256`
values differ between the two sides with BOTH sides non-empty. They are excluded,
and the reason is in `apply_manifest_reconcile`'s docstring: the profile's number
describes the SOURCE file the copier reads and verifies against — a kenney-hq pool
render for 149 of them — while the share's number describes the file already lying
at the destination. Checking the share's bytes proves only that the share is
self-consistent. The pool is not on every machine that runs this script, so the
disagreement is filed rather than guessed.
⛔ DO NOT hand-edit site_a/MANIFEST.json again. It is an OUTPUT. That habit is what
created this document, and `manifest_guard.py` now refuses the run that would have
silently thrown the result away.
